title: Wrap LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl's ledger insert and outbox enqueue in one transaction
why: recordCompletion inserts the learning_ledger row (line 104) and then enqueues its outbox row (line 127) as two separate, unwrapped statements; recordCompletionsBatch commits all N ledger rows inside one _database.transaction() (closes at line 195) but then loops the outbox enqueue afterward, outside that transaction, one row at a time. A process death or crash between these steps leaves a ledger entry (e.g. a manual siyum mark from the Lifetime Marking screen) permanently local-only — nothing re-derives a missing outbox row from an existing ledger row, so it never reaches Firestore or a second device. The sibling CompletionWriter (completion_writer.dart) explicitly wraps its analogous completion_events + outbox insert in one Drift transaction for exactly this reason (its docs call this 'Both rows commit or both roll back' — the FR15/RC1 fix); LearningLedgerRepositoryImpl doesn't follow the same discipline for the same class of append-only sync-critical data.
recommendation: Move the outbox enqueue for recordCompletion inside the same transaction as the ledger insert (or into one atomic Drift batch, as CompletionWriter does); for recordCompletionsBatch, move the per-item enqueueLedgerEntry calls inside the existing transaction block instead of running them afterward in a separate loop.
acceptance_criteria: Both recordCompletion and recordCompletionsBatch write the ledger row(s) and their outbox row(s) inside one transaction; a regression test that fails mid-batch (e.g. a Fake outbox facade that throws after N/2 calls) asserts no ledger row survives without a matching outbox row.

corrections: New evidence beyond the finding: lib/core/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart:11-12/19-20 states insertOutboxRow 'must be called inside the same transaction as the triggering write' — a directly-named invariant, stronger grounds than DB-2 alone. Also: local_data_upload_service.dart:255-259 does re-enqueue every ledger row, but only as a one-time local-to-cloud cutover bridge (story 19.7), not an ongoing safety net — the 'nothing re-derives' claim holds for steady-state usage.
